notes.evidence: valid SSNs and you earned less than $61,555 ($68,675 if married filing jointly),

notes.front: What is the 2025 EIC earned income limit with two qualifying children?
notes.back: Less than $57,310 ($64,430 if married filing jointly).
notes.explanation: It sits between the one-child and three-child limits.
notes.source: Publication 596 (2025), Earned Income Credit, “What’s New”, PDF p. 3
notes.evidence: you have two qualifying children who have valid SSNs and you earned less than $57,310 ($64,430 if married filing jointly)

notes.front: What is the 2025 EIC earned income limit with one qualifying child?
notes.back: Less than $50,434 ($57,554 if married filing jointly).
notes.explanation: The limits rise with the number of children.
notes.source: Publication 596 (2025), Earned Income Credit, “What’s New”, PDF p. 3
notes.evidence: you have one qualifying child who has a valid SSN and you earned less than $50,434 ($57,554 if married filing jointly)

notes.front: What is the 2025 EIC earned income limit with no qualifying child?
notes.back: Less than $19,104 ($26,214 if married filing jointly).
notes.explanation: It is far lower than the limits with children.
notes.source: Publication 596 (2025), Earned Income Credit, “Table 1”, PDF p. 2
notes.evidence: $19,104 ($26,214 for married filing jointly) if you don't have a qualifying child who has a valid SSN.

notes.front: Rosa, head of household, has two qualifying children with valid social security numbers and earned $58,000 in 2025. Can she claim the EIC?
notes.back: B: no; her earnings are not less than $57,310.
notes.choices:
A) Yes
B) No
notes.choicesExplained: A: the two-child limit for her status is $57,310.
notes.source: Publication 596 (2025), Earned Income Credit, “What’s New”, PDF p. 3
notes.evidence: you have two qualifying children who have valid SSNs and you earned less than $57,310 ($64,430 if married filing jointly)

notes.front: A couple filing jointly with three qualifying children earned $66,000 in 2025. Does their income pass the EIC earned income limit?
notes.back: A: yes; $66,000 is less than $68,675.
notes.choices:
A) Yes
B) No
notes.choicesExplained: B applies the $61,555 limit, which is for other filing statuses.
notes.explanation: $66,000 < $68,675 (three or more children, joint).
notes.source: Publication 596 (2025), Earned Income Credit, “What’s New”, PDF p. 3
notes.evidence: valid SSNs and you earned less than $61,555 ($68,675 if married filing jointly),

notes.front: Sam is single with one qualifying child and earned $52,000 in 2025. Does he pass the EIC earned income limit?
notes.back: B: no; $52,000 is not less than $50,434.
notes.choices:
A) Yes
B) No
notes.choicesExplained: A uses a higher limit (two children, or joint).
notes.source: Publication 596 (2025), Earned Income Credit, “What’s New”, PDF p. 3
notes.evidence: you have one qualifying child who has a valid SSN and you earned less than $50,434 ($57,554 if married filing jointly)

notes.front: If an EIC claim is denied for reckless or intentional disregard of the rules, how long is the ban?
notes.back: You can’t claim the EIC for the next 2 years.
notes.explanation: A ban for fraud is longer.
notes.source: Publication 596 (2025), Earned Income Credit, “Chapter 6. Disallowance of the EIC”, PDF p. 22
notes.evidence: that your error was due to reckless or intentional disregard of the EIC rules, then you can't claim the EIC for the next 2 years.

notes.front: If an EIC claim is denied because of fraud, how long is the ban?
notes.back: You can’t claim the EIC for the next 10 years.
notes.explanation: It is five times the ban for reckless or intentional disregard.
notes.source: Publication 596 (2025), Earned Income Credit, “Chapter 6. Disallowance of the EIC”, PDF p. 22
notes.evidence: If your error was due to fraud, then you can't claim the EIC for the next 10 years.

notes.front: The IRS denied Tom’s EIC, finding reckless disregard of the rules (not fraud). For how many following years can’t he claim it?
notes.back: C: 2 years.
notes.choicesExplained: B is not a period used for the EIC ban. C is the ban for fraud.
notes.explanation: Reckless or intentional disregard → 2 years.
notes.source: Publication 596 (2025), Earned Income Credit, “Chapter 6. Disallowance of the EIC”, PDF p. 22
notes.evidence: that your error was due to reckless or intentional disregard of the EIC rules, then you can't claim the EIC for the next 2 years.

notes.front: A taxpayer’s EIC was denied because the claim was fraudulent. How long is the ban?
notes.back: B: 10 years.
notes.choices:
A) 2 years
B) 10 years
C) For life
notes.choicesExplained: A is the ban for reckless or intentional disregard. C: the ban has an end.
notes.explanation: Fraud → 10 years.
notes.source: Publication 596 (2025), Earned Income Credit, “Chapter 6. Disallowance of the EIC”, PDF p. 22
notes.evidence: If your error was due to fraud, then you can't claim the EIC for the next 10 years.

notes.front: Per Pub. 596, what three things is a paid tax preparer?
notes.back: Primarily responsible for the return’s overall substantive accuracy, required to sign it, and required to include their preparer tax identification number.
notes.explanation: Pub. 596 gives these when advising how to choose a preparer.
notes.source: Publication 596 (2025), Earned Income Credit, “Need someone to prepare your tax return?”, PDF p. 25
notes.evidence: A paid tax preparer is: • primarily responsible for the overall substantive accuracy of your return, • required to sign the return, and • required to include their preparer tax identification number (PTIN).

notes.front: A preparer signs a client’s EIC return. The client left out income. Who does Pub. 596 say is ultimately responsible for supplying complete information?
notes.back: C: the taxpayer.
notes.choices:
A) The preparer, who signed
B) The IRS
C) The taxpayer
notes.choicesExplained: A: the preparer signs, but the taxpayer remains ultimately responsible for the information. C has no such role.
notes.explanation: Pub. 596 puts ultimate responsibility on the taxpayer even though the preparer signs.
notes.source: Publication 596 (2025), Earned Income Credit, “Need someone to prepare your tax return?”, PDF p. 25
notes.evidence: Although the tax preparer always signs the return, you're ultimately responsible for providing all the

notes.front: What is the maximum 2025 adoption credit per eligible child?
notes.explanation: The exclusion for employer-provided adoption benefits has the same limit.
notes.source: Publication 17 (2025), Your Federal Income Tax, “Reminders: Adoption credit”, PDF p. 4
notes.evidence: for employer-provided adoption benefits are both $17,280 per eligible child in 2025.

notes.front: From 2025, how much of the adoption credit may be refundable?
notes.back: Up to $5,000, worked out separately for each eligible child.
notes.explanation: Pub. 17 lists this among the adoption credit changes that apply beginning in 2025.
notes.source: Publication 17 (2025), Your Federal Income Tax, “What’s New: Changes to the adoption credit”, PDF p. 4
notes.evidence: Up to $5,000 of your adoption credit may be refundable. The amount of the refundable portion is determined separately for each eligible child.

notes.front: Over what modified AGI range does the 2025 adoption credit phase out?
notes.back: Above $259,190, fully gone at $299,190 or more.
notes.explanation: The range is $40,000 wide.
notes.source: Publication 17 (2025), Your Federal Income Tax, “Reminders: Adoption credit”, PDF p. 4
notes.evidence: The amount begins to phase out if you have modified AGI in excess of $259,190 and is completely phased out if your modified AGI is $299,190 or more.

notes.front: The Browns paid $20,000 of qualified expenses to adopt one child in 2025; modified AGI is $150,000. What is the most adoption credit?
notes.choicesExplained: A exceeds the per-child limit. C is only the refundable part.
notes.explanation: Smaller of $20,000 or $17,280 = $17,280; $150,000 is below the phase-out.
notes.source: Publication 17 (2025), Your Federal Income Tax, “Reminders: Adoption credit”, PDF p. 4
notes.evidence: for employer-provided adoption benefits are both $17,280 per eligible child in 2025.

notes.front: A family with no tax liability qualifies for adoption credits for two eligible children. What is the most that may be refundable?
notes.choicesExplained: A treats the $5,000 as per return. C is the full credit, not the refundable part.
notes.explanation: Refundable part is figured per child: $5,000 × 2 = $10,000.
notes.source: Publication 17 (2025), Your Federal Income Tax, “What’s New: Changes to the adoption credit”, PDF p. 4
notes.evidence: Up to $5,000 of your adoption credit may be refundable. The amount of the refundable portion is determined separately for each eligible child.

notes.front: A couple’s 2025 modified AGI is $305,000. How much adoption credit can they claim?
notes.back: C: none; it is completely phased out at $299,190 or more.
notes.choices:
A) Full credit
B) Reduced credit
C) None
notes.choicesExplained: A and B apply below $299,190.
notes.source: Publication 17 (2025), Your Federal Income Tax, “Reminders: Adoption credit”, PDF p. 4
notes.evidence: is completely phased out if your modified AGI is $299,190 or more.

notes.front: For tax year 2025, can a household with income above 400% of the federal poverty line get the PTC?
notes.back: It may be allowed.
notes.explanation: Pub. 974 lists this under the 2025 applicable percentages.
notes.source: Publication 974 (2025), Premium Tax Credit, “What’s New”, PDF p. 1
notes.evidence: For tax year 2025, taxpayers with household income that exceeds 400% of the federal poverty line for their family size may be allowed a PTC.

notes.front: The Silvas bought 2025 Marketplace coverage; their household income is 450% of the federal poverty line. Are they barred from the PTC by income alone?
notes.back: A: no; for 2025, income above 400% may still be allowed a PTC.
notes.choices:
A) No, they may be allowed a PTC
B) Yes, 400% is a hard ceiling
notes.choicesExplained: A applies a ceiling that Pub. 974 says does not bar 2025 claims.
notes.explanation: 450% exceeds 400%, which for 2025 does not by itself rule out the credit.
notes.source: Publication 974 (2025), Premium Tax Credit, “What’s New”, PDF p. 1
notes.evidence: For tax year 2025, taxpayers with household income that exceeds 400% of the federal poverty line for their family size may be allowed a PTC.

notes.front: What happens if APTC is more than the PTC you are allowed?
notes.back: You have excess APTC and must repay it, subject to certain limitations.
notes.explanation: If APTC is less, you get the difference as a credit.
notes.source: Publication 974 (2025), Premium Tax Credit, “Advance payments of the premium tax credit (APTC)”, PDF p. 3
notes.evidence: If the APTC is more than your PTC, you have excess APTC and you must repay the excess, subject to certain limitations.

notes.front: The Lees’ insurer received $6,000 of APTC in 2025. On Form 8962 their PTC is $4,500. What follows?
notes.back: A: $1,500 of excess APTC, repayable subject to limits.
notes.choices:
A) They have $1,500 excess APTC to repay, subject to limits
B) They get $1,500 more
C) Nothing
notes.choicesExplained: A reverses the comparison. C ignores reconciliation.
notes.explanation: Form 8962 compares the advance payments with the credit allowed: $6,000 less $4,500.
notes.source: Publication 974 (2025), Premium Tax Credit, “Advance payments of the premium tax credit (APTC)”, PDF p. 3
notes.evidence: If the APTC is more than your PTC, you have excess APTC and you must repay the excess, subject to certain limitations.

notes.front: By when should Marketplace enrollees have received Form 1095-A for 2025?
notes.back: By early February 2026.
notes.explanation: Anyone who has not should contact the Marketplace.
notes.source: Publication 974 (2025), Premium Tax Credit, “Useful Items”, PDF p. 3
notes.evidence: you should have received a Form 1095-A by early February 2026.

notes.front: In late February 2026 a client with 2025 Marketplace coverage still has no Form 1095-A. Whom should she contact?
notes.back: A: the Marketplace.
notes.choices:
A) The Marketplace
B) Her employer
C) Her doctor
notes.choicesExplained: B and C don’t issue Form 1095-B.
notes.explanation: Pub. 974 directs people missing the form, or doubting it, to the Marketplace.
notes.source: Publication 974 (2025), Premium Tax Credit, “Useful Items”, PDF p. 3
notes.evidence: Contact your Marketplace if you do not receive a Form 1095-A or if you have questions about the accuracy of your Form 1095-A.

notes.front: After what date can’t residential clean energy credits be claimed for expenditures?
notes.back: Expenditures made after 31 December 2025.
notes.explanation: The credit terminated at the end of 2025.
notes.source: Instructions for Form 5695 (2025), Residential Energy Credits, “What’s New: Termination of credits”, PDF p. 1
notes.evidence: You can't claim residential clean energy credits for expenditures made after December 31, 2025.

notes.front: Which of these is barred from the residential clean energy credit by the termination rule?
notes.back: B: the February 2026 expenditure.
notes.choices:
A) Solar panels paid for in November 2025
B) Solar panels paid for in February 2026
notes.choicesExplained: A was made before the 31 December 2025 cut-off, so the termination does not bar it.
notes.explanation: The bar covers expenditures made after 31 December 2025.
notes.source: Instructions for Form 5695 (2025), Residential Energy Credits, “What’s New: Termination of credits”, PDF p. 1
notes.evidence: You can't claim residential clean energy credits for expenditures made after December 31, 2025.

notes.front: Above what 2025 AGI (Form 1040, line 11a) is a single filer unable to claim the saver’s credit on Form 8880?
notes.explanation: Head of household and joint filers have higher limits.
notes.source: Form 8880 (2025), Credit for Qualified Retirement Savings Contributions, “Form 8880”, PDF p. 1
notes.evidence: is more than $39,500 ($59,250 if head of household; $79,000 if married filing jointly).

notes.front: What is the 2025 saver’s credit AGI limit for head of household?
notes.explanation: It lies between the single and joint limits.
notes.source: Form 8880 (2025), Credit for Qualified Retirement Savings Contributions, “Form 8880”, PDF p. 1
notes.evidence: ($59,250 if head of household; $79,000 if married filing jointly).

notes.front: What is the 2025 saver’s credit AGI limit for married filing jointly?
notes.explanation: It is twice the single limit.
notes.source: Form 8880 (2025), Credit for Qualified Retirement Savings Contributions, “Form 8880”, PDF p. 1
notes.evidence: $79,000 if married filing jointly).

notes.front: Which three kinds of contributor can’t claim the saver’s credit, whatever their income?
notes.back: Someone born after 1 January 2008; someone claimed as a dependent; or a student.
notes.explanation: Form 8880 lists these beside the income test.
notes.source: Form 8880 (2025), Credit for Qualified Retirement Savings Contributions, “Form 8880”, PDF p. 1
notes.evidence: was born after January 1, 2008; (b) is claimed as a dependent on someone else's 2025 tax return; or (c) was a student

notes.front: Tariq, single, 30, not a student, has 2025 AGI of $41,000 and contributed to a retirement plan. Can he claim the saver’s credit?
notes.back: A: no; his AGI is over $39,500.
notes.choices:
A) No
B) Yes
notes.choicesExplained: B: the single limit is $39,500.
notes.source: Form 8880 (2025), Credit for Qualified Retirement Savings Contributions, “Form 8880”, PDF p. 1
notes.evidence: is more than $39,500 ($59,250 if head of household; $79,000 if married filing jointly).

notes.front: Lucy, head of household, 35, not a student, has AGI of $55,000 and made a qualified retirement contribution. Does the income test stop her?
notes.back: A: no; $55,000 is not more than $59,250.
notes.choices:
A) No
B) Yes
notes.choicesExplained: A uses the single limit of $39,500.
notes.source: Form 8880 (2025), Credit for Qualified Retirement Savings Contributions, “Form 8880”, PDF p. 1
notes.evidence: ($59,250 if head of household; $79,000 if married filing jointly).

notes.front: A couple filing jointly has AGI of $80,000 and both contribute to retirement plans. Can they claim the saver’s credit?
notes.back: A: no; $80,000 is more than $79,000.
notes.choices:
A) No
B) Yes
notes.choicesExplained: B: the joint limit is $79,000.
notes.source: Form 8880 (2025), Credit for Qualified Retirement Savings Contributions, “Form 8880”, PDF p. 1
notes.evidence: $79,000 if married filing jointly).

notes.front: How does a tax credit differ from a deduction?
notes.back: A deduction reduces the income subject to tax; a credit directly reduces the tax itself.
notes.explanation: Pub. 970 draws this contrast when introducing the education credits.
notes.source: Publication 970 (2025), Tax Benefits for Education, “Lifetime Learning Credit”, PDF p. 22
notes.evidence: Unlike a deduction, which reduces the amount of income subject to tax, a credit directly reduces the tax itself.

notes.front: Are the child tax credit and the child and dependent care credit the same credit?
notes.back: No: they are separate; the care credit is covered in Pub. 503.
notes.explanation: Pub. 17 warns against confusing them.
notes.source: Publication 17 (2025), Your Federal Income Tax, “Child Tax Credit and Credit for Other Dependents”, PDF p. 111
notes.evidence: The CTC and the ACTC shouldn't be confused with the child and dependent care credit discussed in Pub. 503.
